Subject: Private endpoint networking requirements — StarNet side

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the work to connect StarNet's VPCs to Redwood's private endpoint for our inference workloads. Before we open a ticket with our network team we need a concise list of the expected perimeter controls so we can align our firewall change windows and compliance review. Specifically we need:

- A minimal set of source IPs (or ip ranges) to allow for outbound connections from our NAT/gateway to Redwood's control plane and egress proxies
- Ports and protocols required (TCP/UDP, TLS specifics)
- Whether Redwood supports NATed source IPs (static egress IPs required) or if a mutual TLS-based connection is sufficient
- Any required DNS entries / SRV / CNAME expectations (split-horizon guidance if applicable)
- A short description of audit/logging artifacts Redwood can provide (eg. request IDs, audit logs, retention window) for our security review

We also wanted to know whether you can provide a SOC2 excerpt or security attestation for the private deployment (our auditors asked). If you can send a one-page summary and a recommended firewall rule snippet that our ops team can paste into change requests, that would speed approvals.

Target timeline: we'd like to schedule the change for the week of Feb 23 if we can get the list this week.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — appreciate the clear checklist. High-level answers below; I'll loop in Dev for the low-level NAT/proxy details and Aditya for firewall snippets you can paste into change tickets.

Summary (short):
- Preferred model: customers should use static egress IPs (NAT) from their gateway when possible. Redwood's private endpoint accepts TLS over outbound connections to our control plane and can authenticate via mTLS or API keys depending on the deployment model.
- Ports: outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control plane and egress proxies. Additional ports for metrics/health checks (TCP 9411 for tracing, TCP 2000-2002 for internal metrics collection) are optional and often blocked by customers; we'll note them as optional.
- DNS: we recommend split-horizon DNS for private deployments and will provide the internal CNAMEs you should resolve to the private endpoint IPs.
- Logs: request-level IDs and per-token latency/cost metrics are available through the customer console API. We can provide an audit extract for the onboarding window; retention depends on plan (30/90/365 days).

Action items:
1) Dev — can you confirm the static egress IP ranges we expect customers to pin, and attach the CSV with the reference IP blocks?
2) Aditya — can you draft a short firewall rule snippet (iptables and a cloud-friendly example) and a minimal-change list for StarNet ops?
3) Marissa — I'll prepare a one-page SOC2 excerpt and send it to Alice (redacted as needed).

I'll block 30 mins for a quick alignment call if needed; otherwise please reply inline.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical notes and recommended config. Attached is a CSV with the canonical egress IP ranges we publish for private endpoint customers; please treat the CSV as the single source of truth for change tickets.

Key points:
- Static egress IPs: We strongly recommend customers NAT outbound traffic to a small set of static IP addresses and enter those into their firewall allowlists. This keeps TLS termination straightforward and avoids TLS interception complexity.
- Ports/protocols: 443 (TLS) required. Optional: 9411 (tracing/zipkin), 2000-2002 (internal metrics). Avoid opening 80/8080. UDP is not required.
- Connection patterns: Short-lived TLS sessions; we rely on connection reuse but expect spikes during cold starts. Our runtime is tolerant of transient TCP resets but long pauses will cause request retries.
- DNS: implement split-horizon so that the private endpoint CNAME resolves to your NATed egress public IPs internally, rather than the public Redwood endpoints. If you cannot use split-horizon, pin to the provided IP set in the CSV.
- Proxying: If StarNet environment proxies outbound TLS via an HTTP CONNECT proxy, make sure the proxy preserves the original SNI header. Proxies that terminate TLS (MITM) will break cert chain and require a different trust setup (mutual TLS).

Attached: redwood-egress-reference.csv (contains: service, region, ip_block, last_updated)
Related doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1starnet-integration-docs

--
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Infra — Redwood Inference

Alice — adding the firewall snippets you can paste into your change ticket. Below are two minimal examples: one cloud-native security group style and one iptables snippet for on-prem gateways.

Cloud (example, AWS SG style):
- Inbound: (none required from Redwood)
- Outbound rules (from Gateway/NAT to Redwood):
  * Type: HTTPS, Protocol: TCP, Port Range: 443, Destination: 203.0.113.128/29 (Redwood egress proxy cluster A)
  * Type: HTTPS, Protocol: TCP, Port Range: 443, Destination: 203.0.113.136/29 (Redwood egress proxy cluster B)

Iptables (on-prem gateway):
- Allow outbound TLS to Redwood clusters (replace with CSV ip blocks):
  iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.113.128/29 --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
  iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

Notes:
- If you use a TLS-terminating proxy you must either: (a) configure proxy to passthrough SNI and cert chain to Redwood and avoid rewriting, or (b) use mutual TLS between your proxy and Redwood; we can provide client certs for that path.
- Health check ports (9411) should be optional and limited to internal monitoring subnets; do not open broadly.
- For change ticket descriptions use: "Allow outbound TLS from StarNet NAT to Redwood private egress clusters (see NETOPS-4821). Static egress IPs pinned: redwood-egress-reference.csv"

I'll attach a plain-text file with these snippets for convenience.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Network Engineering
Redwood Inference
